    <h1 class="devsite-page-title" tabindex="-1">
      Use Gemini Code Assist code customization<devsite-actions hidden data-nosnippet><devsite-feature-tooltip
      ack-key="AckCollectionsBookmarkTooltipDismiss"
      analytics-category="Site-Wide Custom Events"
      analytics-action-show="Callout Profile displayed"
      analytics-action-close="Callout Profile dismissed"
      analytics-label="Create Collection Callout"
      class="devsite-page-bookmark-tooltip nocontent"
      data-nosnippet
      dismiss-button="true"
      id="devsite-collections-dropdown"
      
      dismiss-button-text="Dismiss"

      
      close-button-text="Got it">

    
    
      <devsite-bookmark></devsite-bookmark>

    </span>

  <div class="devsite-article-body clearfix
  ">

  
    
    
    
    

<p>This document describes how to use
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/code-customization-overview">Gemini Code Assist code customization</a>
and provides a few best practices. This feature lets you receive code
recommendations, which draw from the internal libraries, private APIs, and the
coding style of your organization.</p>

<h2 id="before_you_begin" data-text="Before you begin" tabindex="-1">Before you begin</h2>

<ol>
<li><p><a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/set-up-gemini">Set up Gemini Code Assist</a>
with an <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview#supported-features">Enterprise subscription</a>.</p></li>
<li><p><a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/code-customization">Set up Gemini Code Assist code customization</a>.</p></li>
</ol>

<h2 id="how-to-use" data-text="How to use code customization" tabindex="-1">How to use code customization</h2>

<p>The following table lists ways to use
Gemini Code Assist code customization:</p>

<table>
   <thead>
      <th width="20%">Form</th>
      <th width="40%">How to trigger</th>
      <th>Notes and resources</th>
   </thead>
   <tr>
      <td><p>Natural language chat</p>
      </td>
      <td>
        <p>Enter a natural language prompt in Gemini Code Assist
        chat in the IDE.</p></td>
      <td><p>Consider the following:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>Chat history is not available. Avoid multi-step queries.</li>
            <li>You can ask for more details about sources, including links to
            the specific sources.</li>
            <li>If you highlight or select code when you send a message in chat,
            Gemini Code Assist uses that code to improve code
            customization and chat quality.</li>
         </ul>
         <p>For more information, see
         <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/chat-overview">Chat with Gemini Code Assist</a>.
         </p>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Generate code</td>
      <td>In the quick pick bar in your IDE, either with or without
        selected code, press <kbd>Command+Enter</kbd> (on macOS) or
        <kbd>Control+Enter</kbd>.</td>
      <td>For more information, see
        <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/write-code-gemini#generate_code_with_prompts">Generate code with prompts</a>.
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Transform code</td>
      <td>In the quick pick bar in your IDE, either with or without
        selected code, enter <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/fix</code>.</td>
      <td>For more information, see
        <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/write-code-gemini#generate_code_with_prompts">Generate code with prompts</a>.
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Autocomplete</td>
      <td>Code customization is automatically triggered and provides
        suggestions based on what you write.</td>
      <td><p>Consider the following:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>Code completion needs a certain level of confidence to propose a
            suggestion. Ensure that a substantial amount of code is available
            so that relevant snippets are retrieved.</li>
            <li>Code completion checks if you have required libraries in order
            to use certain elements of the function.</li>
         </ul>
         <p>For more information, see
         <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/write-code-gemini#get_code_completions">Get code completions</a>.
         </p>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Remote repository context</td>
      <td>
         <ol>
         <li>Start your prompt with the <kbd>@</kbd> symbol. A list of available remote
          repositories that are indexed appears.</li>
         <li>Select the repository you want to use for context from the list.
          You can also start typing the repository name to filter the list.</li>
         <li>After selecting the repository, write the rest of your prompt.</li>
         </ol>
      </td>
      <td><p>Remote repository context is useful when you are working on a task
         that is mostly related to a specific set of microservices, libraries,
         or modules.</p>
         <p>For more information, see
         <a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/write-code-gemini#get_more_relevant_suggestions_with_remote_repository_context">Get more relevant suggestions with remote repository context</a>.
         </p>
      </td>
   </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="use-cases" data-text="Use cases and prompt examples" tabindex="-1">Use cases and prompt examples</h2>

<p>The following table provides guidance and examples about using
code customization in specific use cases:</p>

<table>
   <thead>
      <th width="20%">Use case</th>
      <th>Things worth trying</th>
   </thead>
   <tr>
      <td>Writing new code</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following to generate code in your IDE or
         Gemini Code Assist chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>Generate code that would use terms which are already mentioned
            in your codebase.</li>
            <li>Paste in your code, such as a functional signature or code with
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr">TODO</code> comments, and then ask
            Gemini Code Assist to fill in or replace
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr">TODO</code> comments with code. Add comments with explanation
            from context.</li>
         </ul>
         <p>Try generating code with the following prompts in
         Gemini Code Assist chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Write a main function where a connection to
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">DATABASE</var></code> is created. Include health
            checks."</li>
            <li>"Write a <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_OR_CLASS</var></code> in the
            following structure:
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">EXPLAIN_STRUCTURE</var></code>."</li>
         </ul>
         <p>After you generate some code, try using a follow-up prompt to
         improve it:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Try the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/fix</code> command to adjust the generated
            code—for example, syntax errors."</li>
            <li>"Add missing imports."</li>
            <li>"Try <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/fix</code> on chat-generated code."</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Cleaning, simplifying, and refactoring code</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Can you merge
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">IMPORTS_VARIABLES_OR_NOTE_EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS</var></code>
            in this file?"</li>
            <li>"How would you simplify the
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code> function?"</li>
            <li>"Can you merge <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME_1</var></code> and
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME_2</var></code> into one function?"</li>
            <li>"Could you inline some variables in
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>?"</li>
            <li>"Could you simplify variable naming in the function
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>?"</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Readability</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Write the function <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code> in
            fewer lines of code, if possible."</li>
            <li>"Add comments to the function
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>."</li>
            <li>"Remove unnecessary whitespaces in the function
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>."</li>
            <li>"Format the function <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code> in a
            similar way as the rest of the code."</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Code review</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Split the code in parts and explain each part using our
            codebase."</li>
            <li>"Are there variables or keywords that could be shorter and more
            self-explanatory?"</li>
            <li>"Can you give me useful code from the
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_NAME_PACKAGE_MODULE</var></code> context for
            this code?"</li>
            <li>"What do you think about the function
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>?"</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Debugging</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"I am getting an error when I try to do X/add Y. Why?"</li>
            <li>"Can you spot an error in the function
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>?"</li>
            <li>"How would you fix the function
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code> given this error
            message?"</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Learning and onboarding</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Split this code in parts and explain each of them using our
            codebase."</li>
            <li>"Show how to call function
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>?"</li>
            <li>"Show how to run the main function in the
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">ENVIRONMENT_NAME</var></code> environment?"</li>
            <li>"What is the key technical improvement we can do to make this
            code more performant?"</li>
            <li>"Show me the implementation of
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_OR_CLASS_NAME</var></code> to achieve better
            results and add what that specific element is"—for example,
            "Show me the implementation of function foo where foo is the name of
            the function."</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Migration</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Give me a strategy for how I can migrate
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FILE_NAME</var></code> from
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">LANGUAGE_1</var></code> to
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">LANGUAGE_2</var></code>"—for example, from Go to
            Python.</li>
            
            <li>"Given the function <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code> in
            repository <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_NAME</var></code>, find me an
            equivalent function in language
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">LANGUAGE_NAME</var></code> that I can use."</li>
         </ul>
         <p>Try the following chat-based or code generation transformation
         workflow using prompts:</p>
         <ol>
            <li>"Take <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FILENAME_COMPONENT</var></code> code
            already written in <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">LANGUAGE_1</var></code> and refactor
            and migrate it to <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">LANGUAGE_2</var></code>"—for example,
            from Go to Python.</li>
            <li>After you migrate some code, try the following:
               <ul>
                  <li>Select smaller chunks and use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/fix</code> to get
                  it into a state that you want.</li>
                  <li>Try the following prompts:</li>
                  <ul>
                     <li>"Is there something which can be improved?"</li>
                     <li>"Give me possible pain points."</li>
                     <li>"How would you test this code if that migration is
                     correct?"</li>
                  </ul>
               </ul>
            </li>
         </ol>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Generating documentation</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Summarize the code in package or folder
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">X</var></code> and provide documentation for the top five
            important methods."</li>
            <li>"Generate documentation for
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_OR_CLASS_NAME</var></code>."</li>
            <li>"Shorten the documentation while preserving the key
            information."</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
   <tr>
      <td>Unit test generation</td>
      <td>
         <p>Try the following prompts in Gemini Code Assist
         chat:</p>
         <ul>
            <li>"Generate unit tests for <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FILENAME</var></code>."</li>
            <li>"Add the most relevant test cases for the
            <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code> function."</li>
            <li>"Remove test cases that you think don't bring much value."</li>
         </ul>
      </td>
   </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="best_practices" data-text="Best practices" tabindex="-1">Best practices</h2>

<ul>
<li><strong>Use relevant variable and function names or code snippets.</strong> This guides
code customization towards the most pertinent code examples.</li>
<li><strong>Use index repositories that you want to scale, and avoid adding deprecated
functionality.</strong> Code customization helps to scale to the code style,
patterns, code semantics, knowledge, and implementations across the codebase.
Bad examples of repositories to scale are deprecated functionalities,
generated code, and legacy implementations.</li>
<li><strong>For code retrieval use cases, use code generation functionality instead of
code completion</strong>. Prompt using language such as &quot;Using the definition of
<code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>, generate the exact same function,&quot; or
&quot;Generate the exact implementation of <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">FUNCTION_NAME</var></code>.&quot;</li>
<li><strong>Have includes or imports present in the file for the code that you want to
retrieve</strong> to improve Gemini contextual awareness.</li>
<li><strong>Execute only one action for each prompt.</strong> For example, if you want to
retrieve code and have this code be implemented in a new function, perform
these steps over two prompts.</li>
<li><strong>For use cases where you want more than just code</strong> (such as code
explanation, migration plan, or error explanation), use
code customization for chat, where you have a conversation with
Gemini with your codebase in context.</li>
<li><strong>Note that AI model generation is non-deterministic</strong>. If you aren&#39;t
satisfied with the response, executing the same prompt again might achieve a
better result.</li>
<li><strong>Note that generating unit tests</strong> generally works better if you open the
file locally, and then from chat, ask to generate unit tests for this file or
a specific function.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="get_more_relevant_suggestions_with_remote_repository_context" data-text="Get more relevant suggestions with remote repository context" tabindex="-1"><strong>Get more relevant suggestions with remote repository context</strong></h3>

<p>You can get more contextually aware and relevant code suggestions by directing Gemini Code Assist to focus on specific remote repositories. By using the <kbd>@</kbd> symbol in the chat, you can select one or more repositories to be used as a primary source of context for your prompts. This is useful when you are working on a task that is mostly related to a specific set of microservices, libraries, or modules.</p>

<p>To use a remote repository as context, follow these steps in your IDE&#39;s chat:</p>

<ol>
<li>Start your prompt with the <kbd>@</kbd> symbol. A list of available remote repositories that are indexed will appear.</li>
<li>Select the repository you want to use for context from the list. You can also start typing the repository name to filter the list.</li>
<li>After selecting the repository, write the rest of your prompt.</li>
</ol>

<p>Gemini will then prioritize the selected repository when generating a response.</p>

<h4 id="example_prompts" data-text="Example Prompts" tabindex="-1"><strong>Example Prompts</strong></h4>

<p>Here are some examples of how you can use this feature:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>To understand a repository:</strong>
<ul>
<li>&quot;<kbd>@</kbd><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_NAME</var></code> What is the overall structure of this repository?&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;<kbd>@</kbd><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_NAME</var></code> I&#39;m a new team member. Can you give me an overview of this repository&#39;s purpose and key modules?&quot;</li>
</ul></li>
<li><strong>For code generation and modification:</strong>
<ul>
<li>&quot;<kbd>@</kbd><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_NAME</var></code> Implement an authentication function similar to the one in this repository.&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;<kbd>@</kbd><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_NAME</var></code> Refactor the following code to follow the conventions in the selected repository.&quot;</li>
<li>&quot;<kbd>@</kbd><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_A_NAME</var></code> How can I use the latest functions from this repository to improve my code in <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">REPOSITORY_B_NAME</var></code>?&quot;</li>
</ul></li>
<li><strong>For testing:</strong>
<ul>
<li>&quot;<kbd>@</kbd><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">UNIT_TEST_FILE_NAME</var></code> Generate unit tests for <code translate="no" dir="ltr"><var translate="no">MODULE</var></code> based on the examples in the selected file.&quot;</li>
</ul></li>
</ul>

<p>By using remote repositories as a focused source of context, you can get more accurate and relevant suggestions from Gemini Code Assist, which can help you code faster and more efficiently.</p>
